remain-stationary.name: Remain Stationary
remain-stationary.body:
This Action can only be used by a unit as its first Action. The selected unit entrenches itself in a secure, defensible position. No Actions aside from Shoot or Mission Task can be used as part the unit's Activation thereafter. A unit that chose to Remain Stationary increases its Initiative characteristic by 1 until the end of the Battle Round.
Units that use this Action while wholly positioned in a terrain feature with the Light Cover or Heavy Cover keywords, and then do not complete a Shoot Action afterwards, gain the Stealth ability.

move.name: Move
move.body:
The unit may Move up to the maximum Movement characteristic detailed on its datasheet, and in accordance with any applicable Keywords impacting how that unit can move (for example, weapons with the Heavy keyword).
This Action cannot be used under the following conditions:
• Your unit is within Base-to-base contact of any enemy models.
• Your unit has already used this Action once as part of its activation.

advance.name: Advance
advance.body:
Units can choose to Advance immediately after completing a Move Action. An Advance is additional movement completed as follows:
• The unit completes its Advance movement up to a distance in inches equal to the lowest Initiative value in that unit.
• Units that Advance are not eligible to Shoot with any weapons other than weapons that possess the Pistol or Assault keyword.
• Units that Advance are not eligible to Charge and Fight, unless they possess an ability or model keyword (such as Relentless) that enables them to do so.

fall-back.name: Fall Back
fall-back.body: The selected unit may Fall Back as its first Action if it begins its Activation within Base-to-Base Contact of enemy models. It may Fall Back up to the maximum Movement characteristic detailed on its datasheet, and must not end this Fall Back move closer to any enemy models than when it began. Units that Fall Back cannot then use remaining Activation Points for any of the following actions: Move, Shoot, and Charge and Fight, unless that unit has access to abilities or Stratagems that allow it to complete other Actions after making a Fall Back Action.

enter-the-battlefield-from-strategic-res.name: Enter the Battlefield from Strategic Reserves
enter-the-battlefield-from-strategic-res.body: Units held in Strategic Reserves may enter the battlefield as their first Action. Units that do count as having completed a Move Action and may not then Move, but can otherwise act normally.

embark-or-disembark-from-a-transport.name: Embark or Disembark from a Transport
embark-or-disembark-from-a-transport.body:
This Action is utilized by the selected unit in one of several ways:
Disembark: If the selected unit is currently embarked in a Transport, it can use this Action to Disembark from that Transport unit. Models that disembark must first be placed within 3" of the Transport unit before spending any more Activation Points.
• Units that Disembark from a Transport that has not yet been activated this turn may then use their remaining Activation Points to complete any of the following eligible Actions: Move, Shoot, Mission Task, Charge and Fight, adhering to any limitations to the sequencing of those activations where applicable. Disembarking under this condition costs 1 Activation Point.
• Units that Disembark from a Transport that has used the Move Action this Battle Round may not use the Charge and Fight Action, unless that Transport has the Assault Egress keyword, but can otherwise act normally. Disembarking under this condition costs 2 Activation Points.
• Units can never disembark from a Transport that has used the Advance Action.
Embark: If all models in the selected unit are within 3" of a friendly Transport, it may use this Action to embark into that Transport. It may then no longer use any remaining Activation Points, unless that Transport possesses unique abilities that allow units to function while embarked (ie, making Ranged attacks via the Firing Deck [X] ability). Embarking always costs 1 Activation Point.
Emergency Disembarkation: When a Transport is destroyed, every unit embarked within it at that time must immediately make an Emergency Disembarkation. To do so, Roll 1 D6 for each model in the unit. For each roll of a 1 - or a roll of a 1 or 2 if the Transport being destroyed triggered the Deadly Demise [X] ability - the unit suffers 1 Mortal Wound. Models not destroyed at this stage are then placed within 3" of the Transport model. The unit then takes a Battle Shock Test, or is automatically considered to be Battle Shocked if the Transport being destroyed triggered the Deadly Demise [X] ability.

shoot.name: Shoot
shoot.body: The selected unit may make Ranged attacks with all models in the unit eligible to do so. Units that Shoot may then spend remaining Activation Points on any other Actions, but must follow any Action restrictions affecting that unit caused by relevant Keywords (ie, Heavy, Ordnance).

charge-and-fight.name: Charge and Fight
charge-and-fight.body:
This Action is completed as follows:
• The selected unit Charges an enemy unit (or units) by moving a charge move distance in Inches equal to D6 + the lowest Initiative characteristic in the unit. At least 1 model from the unit must be able to get into Base-to-Base Contact with a model from the enemy unit being Charged in order for the Charge to be considered successful.
• Resolve Melee attacks using the Fight Order of Operations detailed under the Making Attacks section of the Core Rules. The unit that completed this Charge and Fight Action increases their Initiative value by 1 for this Fight.
If the selected unit has any remaining Activation Points after completing the Charge and Fight Activation, and there are no longer any enemy models within Base-to-Base contact with any models in the unit, it may then continue to spend them on the following eligible Actions: Move, Shoot, Embark or Disembark from a Transport.

fight.name: Fight
fight.body:
The selected unit may Fight, following the order of operations described under the Melee Attacks rules section, under 1 of the 2 following scenarios:
• As part of the unit's own Activation if it has models is within Base-to-base contact with enemy models when it is Activated, using its first Activation Point. Units selected to use the Fight Action in this manner may then spend any remaining Activation Points on other eligible Actions, excluding the following: Embark or Disembark from a Transport, Enter the Battlefield from Strategic Reserves, and Charge and Fight. Units cannot use this Action if they have already used the Charge and Fight Action during the current Battle Round.
• When it is the target of an enemy unit's Charge and Fight Action, wherein this Action does not cost the unit an Activation Point because it is must complete this Action as part of that enemy unit's Charge and Fight Action.

ascend-to-the-skies.name: Ascend to the Skies
ascend-to-the-skies.body: This Action can only be used by units with at least one of the following keywords: Aircraft, Fly, or Jump Pack. Remove the unit from the table and place it into Strategic Reserves.

return-to-the-shadows.name: Return to the Shadows
return-to-the-shadows.body:
This Action is only available to be used through Faction or Unit abilities that explicitly state it can be used.
A unit can use the following Action if satisfies all of the following conditions:
• Already completed either a Move or Shoot Action as part of its Activation, but no other Actions
• Is wholly within 3" of a Terrain Feature
• Is more than 6" away from any enemy models
When it does so, remove the unit from the table and place it into Strategic Reserves.

mission-task.name: Mission Task
mission-task.body:
This Action allows the unit to complete any Mission Task as determined by an active Primary or Secondary Objective.
Units cannot select this Action if any models in the unit are in Base-to-Base contact with any enemy models. Further this Action can only be used by a unit if that unit did not yet use any of the following Actions as part of this Activation: Shoot, Charge and Fight, Fight, Fall Back.
Battleline units that use this Action cannot then be selected for a Bonus Activation during the current Battle Round.

hold-fast.name: Hold Fast
hold-fast.body:
This Action allows the unit to effectively 'pass' on being Activated this Battle Round. The unit must declare it will Hold Fast at the start of its Activation, and cannot use any subsequent Actions under any conditions whatsoever. This Action cannot be used if the unit is:
• In Base-to-Base Contact with any enemy units, or,
• Has any models within 6" of any enemy units.
Units that Hold Fast are not eligible to complete a Bonus Activation this Battle Round.

infantry.name: Infantry
infantry.body:
Infantry models must abide by the following when completing the Move or Charge and Fight Actions:
• Treat any terrain feature that is less than 1" tall as if it was not there. However, moving over terrain features that are 1" or taller must be factored into the model's movement as vertical distance it must travel.
• Reduce their Movement characteristic by 2" when entering or exiting a terrain feature with the Building keyword. This is to represent models spending their energy finding safe entry points breaching through walls, or clambering over debris. Move Actions that begin and end within a terrain feature with the Building keyword are not subject to this constraint, but are subject to vertical terrain feature measuring detailed above.
When Infantry models used the Shoot Action, they can choose to target more than 1 enemy unit if they possess more than 1 Ranged weapon. However, the attacking player can only choose 1 target to attack at the model's full Ballistic Skill. Ranged attacks against each additional unit targeted reduces the model's Ballistic Skill by 1. These reductions are applied in the order that the player chooses to make their attacks (i.e., the first weapon fired will have full Ballistic Skill, the second will have Ballistic Skill -1, the third will have Ballistic Skill -2, and so on).
Infantry models' Objective Control (OC) value is equal to their Toughness characteristic.

vehicle.name: Vehicle
vehicle.body:
Vehicle models must abide by the following when completing a Move, Advance or Charge and Fight Action:
• The model must always move forwards or backwards relative to the front of the vehicle's hull (use reasonable logic to identify this based on the design of the vehicle!). When completing any form of Movement, a Vehicle must decide whether it will turn or pivot as part of its movement, or go in a straight line relative to the front of the model's hull. If the model will turn or pivot, reduce its Movement characteristic by 2".
• The model cannot move over any terrain features that are more than 2" tall relative to the ground, unless benefitting from another keyword such as Fly that allows the model to ignore vertical movement distances.
• The model may only enter terrain by completing a Breach test. To complete a Breach test, roll a D6. On a 4+ the Vehicle successfully breaches the terrain and can be moved into or through that terrain feature. A Vehicle with a Toughness characteristic of 12 or above reduces its Breach test to 3+.
• Reduce their Movement characteristic by 2" when moving into or through a terrain feature This is additional over any reductions to the Movement characteristic associated with turning or pivoting, as detailed above.
Vehicle models that are in Base-to-Base Contact with enemy models never need to use the Fall Back Action. Instead, Vehicle models can simply complete a Move Action to leave Base-to-Base Contact. When doing so, a Vehicle model can be moved over enemy models, but must reduce its Movement characteristic by 2".
When using the Shoot Action, Vehicle models:
• Are always considered to possess the Implacable ability.
• Can make Ranged attacks with any number of Ranged weapons they are equipped with and may target any number of enemy units as chosen by the attacking player.
• Can select enemy units with models in Base-to-Base contact as the target of a Ranged attack, but reduce their Hit rolls by 1 when doing so.
When making a Ranged attack against a Vehicle, that Vehicle is:
• Always considered to have a Ballistic Skill of 3.
• Eligible to be the target of a Ranged attack even whilst it is in Base-to-Base contact with other models.
• Subject to the "Hit Them From Behind!" rule, if applicable, as detailed under Making Attacks.
When making Ranged or Melee attacks within 3" of a Vehicle, do not make a Hit Roll. Such attacks are automatically considered a Critical Hit. This does not apply to Vehicle models that also possess the Walker keyword.
Vehicle models that are reduced to 1/3 of their Starting Strength (rounding down) reduce their:
• Activation Points by 1
• Hit rolls by 1
• Movement characteristic by 4"
For determining the Objective Control (OC) value of a Vehicle:
• Models with a Toughness characteristic up to 11 have an OC value equal to their remaining Wounds characteristic
• Models with a Toughness characteristic of 11 or higher have an OC value equal to double their remaining Wounds characteristic
When a Vehicle model is destroyed and does not suffer the effects of the Deadly Demise [X] keyword, the controlling player must replace that model with an equivalently sized Wreckage terrain feature. If such a terrain feature is not available, the player must instead use the vehicle itself, and ideally add some small visual indicator - such as a 'Destroyed - Wreckage' token, a cotton ball to represent smoke, or a misplaced element of the model (such as its turret) - to remind players that the model has been destroyed.

monster.name: Monster
monster.body:
Monster models must abide by the following when completing a Move, Advance or Charge and Fight Action:
• The model may only enter terrain by completing a Breach test. To complete a Breach test, roll a D6. On a 4+ the Monster successfully breaches the terrain and can be moved into or through that terrain feature. A Monster with a Toughness characteristic of 12 or above reduces the Breach test to 3+.
• Reduce their Movement characteristic by 2" when moving into or through a terrain feature This is additional over any reductions to the Movement characteristic associated with turning or pivoting, as detailed above.
• Cannot move more than 4" vertically through any terrain feature, unless benefitting from another keyword such as Fly that allows the model to ignore vertical movement distances.
Monster models that are in Base-to-Base Contact with enemy models never need to use the Fall Back Action. Instead, Monster models can simply complete a Move Action to leave Base-to-Base Contact. When doing so, a Monster model can be moved over enemy models, but must reduce its Movement characteristic by 2".
When using the Shoot Action, Monster models:
• Are always considered to possess the Implacable ability.
• Can make Ranged attacks with any number of Ranged weapons they are equipped with and may target any number of enemy units as chosen by the attacking player.
• Can select enemy units with models in Base-to-Base contact as the target of a Ranged attack, but reduce their Hit rolls by 1 when doing so.
When making a Ranged attack against a Monster, that Monster is:
• Always considered to have a Ballistic Skill of 3.
• Eligible to be the target of a Ranged attack even whilst it is in Base-to-Base contact with other models.
• Subject to the "Hit Them From Behind!" rule, if applicable, as detailed under Making Attacks.
Monster models that are reduced to 1/3 of their Starting Strength (rounding down) reduce their:
• Activation Points by 1
• Hit rolls by 1
• Movement characteristic by 4"
For determining the Objective Control (OC) value of a Monster:
• Models with a Toughness characteristic up to 11 have an OC value equal to their remaining Wounds characteristic
• Models with a Toughness characteristic of 11 or higher have an OC value equal to double their remaining Wounds characteristic

beast.name: Beast
beast.body:
Beast models must abide by the following when completing a Move, Advance or Charge and Fight Action:
• Treat any terrain feature that is less than 2" tall as if it was not there.
• Cannot enter terrain features with the Building keyword unless they pass a Breach test. To complete a Breach test, roll a D6. On a 4+ the Beast successfully breaches the terrain and can be moved into or through that terrain feature.
Beast models' Objective Control (OC) value is equal to their Toughness characteristic.

battleline.name: Battleline
battleline.body:
Up to 2 of each unit with the Battleline keyword can be taken in your army for every 500 points. Battleline units are also eligible to make Bonus Activations, may be eligible for other Mission-specific rules, and often have interactions with faction-specific Army Rules and abilities.
Models with the Battleline keyword increase their Objective Control (OC) value by 1.

character.name: Character
character.body:
Up to 1 of each unit with the Character keyword can be taken in your army for every 1,000 points.
Models with the Character keyword can only be selected as the subject of an attack under the following conditions:
• The model is the closest model to the attacking unit when making a Ranged attack, and is not within 3" of any other friendly Units.
• The model is in base-to-base contact with the attacking model when making a Melee attack.
• The attacking model has the Precision ability.
The conditions above do not apply to Character units that also possess any of the following model type keywords: Vehicle, Monster.
Models with the Character keyword multiply their Objective Control (OC) value by 2.

leader.name: Leader
leader.body:
Your army must include at least 1 Leader model.
Models with the Leader keyword can choose to lead a friendly Unit. The Units that the Leader is eligible to lead are listed on its Unit Profile. Leader models and friendly Units they are leading is determined during your Pregame Setup, before the units are placed on the battlefield, and before the decision to declare that those units are either embarked in a Transport, or placed into Strategic Reserve.
Leader models and the Unit they are leading count as a single unit for Activation purposes, and when an enemy unit selects them as the subject of an attack. If a Leader model's Activation Points characteristic is different from that of the unit they are leading, players use the Leader's Activation Points characteristic when Activating that unit.

bodyguard.name: Bodyguard
bodyguard.body: Models with the Bodyguard keyword must always take damage from attacks - and be destroyed - before any other models in the unit suffer damage. This includes when a unit includes a Character keyword, or when attacks made against the unit include the Precision ability.

epic-hero.name: Epic Hero
epic-hero.body:
Your army can only ever include 1x of each unit with the Epic Hero keyword.
Models with the Epic Hero keyword increase their Objective Control (OC) value by 3.

walker.name: Walker
walker.body:
Models with the Walker keyword must abide by the following when completing a Move, Advance or Charge and Fight Action:
• Do not need to reduce their Movement characteristic when making a turn or a pivot.
• The model may only enter terrain by completing a Breach test. To complete a Breach test, roll a D6. On a 2+ the Walker successfully breaches the terrain and can be moved into or through that terrain feature.
• Cannot move more than 4" vertically through any terrain feature, unless the model possesses other keywords (such as Fly or Jump Pack) that enable it to do so.
Walker models always possess the Implacable ability.

mounted.name: Mounted
mounted.body:
Models with the Mounted keyword must abide by the following when completing a Move Action:
• The model must always move forwards relative to the front of the model's body (typically identified by the direction its head is facing, or equivalent feature such as hull front).
• When completing any form of Movement, a Mounted model must decide whether it will turn or pivot as part of its movement, or go in a straight line relative to the front of the model's body. If the model will turn or pivot, reduce its Movement characteristic by 2".
• Cannot enter terrain features with the Building keyword.
• Cannot move more than 4" vertically through any terrain feature.

psyker.name: Psyker
psyker.body:
Many units in Alt-Hammer have psychic abilities drawn from the powers of the Warp. These units always possess the Psyker keyword, typically possess Special Abilities marked as [Psychic], and can typically access Psychic-type Ranged attacks.
Using any Psychic abilities or Psychic weapons requires first taking a Psychic Test, which follows these steps:
• Each time a unit uses its [Psychic] ability or makes a Psychic weapon, the controlling player first rolls 2D6.
• The specific [Psychic] ability will describe when that ability is used (i.e., during your Command Phase, or when the unit is Activated)
• If the result of the roll is higher than the model's Leadership characteristic, the Psychic Test is passed, and the [Psychic] ability or Psychic attack can proceed as normal.
• If the result of the roll is lower than the model's Leadership characteristic, the Psychic Test is failed, and the [Psychic] ability or Psychic attack cannot be used.
• If the result of the roll is either two 1s or two 6s (i.e., a total value of 2 or 12), the unit suffers Perils of the Warp and immediately takes 2D3 Mortal Wounds.
• If the roll was a 2, the [Psychic] ability or Psychic attack cannot be used.
• If the roll was a 12, the [Psychic] ability or Psychic attack can be used, but must target the closest unit - friendly or enemy.
• If the unit suffering Perils of the Warp is destroyed as a result of the Mortal Wounds inflicted, that unit is considered to have the Deadly Demise D3+1 ability.
Note that some faction rules or unit special abilities may impact the results of Psychic Tests, or create requirements for a Psyker to take additional Psychic Tests even when not making Psychic attacks or using [Psychic] abilities.

implacable.name: Implacable
implacable.body:
Infantry Models with this ability:
• Always use their full Ballistic Skill characteristic if the model possesses the Infantry keyword
• Ignore all effects of the Heavy keyword
Note that models with any of the following keywords are always considered to have the Implacable ability: Vehicle, Monster and Walker.

small-profile.name: Small Profile
small-profile.body: Small Profile models add 1 to their Toughness characteristic when they are the target of a Ranged attack. Additionally, these models gain the Invulnerable Save 4+ ability against Ranged attacks when wholly positioned in a terrain feature with the Light Cover or Heavy Cover keywords.

phase-shift.name: Phase Shift
phase-shift.body: Models with this ability can move horizontally through any model or Terrain Feature as if it was not there.

hover.name: Hover
hover.body: Models with the Hover keyword treat any terrain feature that is less than 4" tall as if it was not there and are not required to reduce their Movement characteristic when completing any movement that includes a turn or pivot if the model also has other Model Type keywords (such as Vehicle, Monster, and Mounted) that would require it to do so. Any other restrictions movement actions determined by other keywords the model has are still in effect.

jump-pack.name: Jump Pack
jump-pack.body: When completing either a Move, Advance or Charge and Fight Action, models with the Jump Pack keyword can ignore any terrain features that are less than 8" tall.

fly.name: Fly
fly.body:
When completing either a Move, Advance or Charge and Fight Action, models with the Fly keyword:
• Can ignore any terrain features that are less than 8" tall.
• Do not need to make a Breaching Test to enter terrain features with the Building keyword if another keyword the model possesses typically requires that they do so (ie, Vehicle or Monster).
• Are not required to reduce their Movement characteristic when making a Move action that includes a turn or pivot if the model also has other Model Type keywords (such as Vehicle, Monster, and Mounted) that would require it to do so.
Further, enemy units making a Ranged attack against a model with the Fly keyword reduce their Hit rolls by 1 if the model has already completed a Move action during the current Battle Round, and that Move Action resulted in the model ending its move more than 12" horizontally from its original position on the battlefield.

aircraft.name: Aircraft
aircraft.body:
Models with the Aircraft keyword have two values in their Movement characteristic: [X]"-[Y]". [X]" is the minimum value this model must move, and [Y]" is the maximum value this model can move.
Additionally, models with the Aircraft keyword:
• Cannot elect to Remain Stationary when it is Activated, unless the model also possesses the Hover keyword.
• Are not required to reduce their Movement characteristic when making a Move action that includes a turn or pivot (a limitation that is imposed by other Model Type keywords such as Vehicle, Monster). However, an Aircraft cannot turn or pivot more than 90 degrees in a single move unless the following 2 conditions are met:
• The model possesses the Hover keyword.
• The model moved more than 16"
• Are always treated as being fully visible to attacking enemy units making Ranged attacks, even if the Aircraft's position on the board is physically obscured.
• Are always able to draw line of sight to an enemy unit they target for a Ranged attack. When making these attacks, weapons gain the Ignores Cover ability.
• Can never benefit from Light Cover or Heavy Cover.
• Cannot be the target of an enemy unit's Charge and Fight Action unless that enemy unit has the Fly or Jump Pack keywords.
• Cannot use the following Actions: Fight and Charge and Fight.
Further, enemy units making a Ranged attack against a model with the Aircraft keyword reduce their Hit rolls by 1 if the model has already completed a Move action during the current Battle Round, and that Move Action resulted in the model ending its move more than 12" horizontally from its original position on the battlefield.
Models with the Aircraft keyword always possess an OC value of 0, and can never increase their OC value above 0.

titanic.name: Titanic
titanic.body:
Model with the Titanic keyword:
• Can only be included in your army in battles that are 1,500 points or more. In such battles, you can include 1 of each Titanic unit for every 1,000 points in battle size.
• Can never benefit from Light Cover or Heavy Cover.
• Cannot benefit from the Obscuring keyword while any part of the model is visible to an attacking enemy model using true line of sight.
• Treat the Ordnance wargear ability as if it was the Heavy wargear ability when making Ranged attacks.
• Can move through terrain features unless that terrain feature has the Impassable keyword. When they do so, reduce their Movement characteristic by 4".
• After a model with the Titanic keyword has moved through a terrain feature, remove that terrain feature from the tabletop and replace it with a terrain feature (or area marker) that represents Difficult Ground only, unless the terrain feature has the Hill keyword. This is to reflect the total destructive impact of such a large machine or creature traversing any physical structures, vegetation, or other objects.
• Can move over and passed enemy and friendly models as if they were not there. Additionally, when making a move passed models, or ending a move within Base-to-base contact of a model (ie, as part of a Charge and Fight Action), roll a D6 for each such model. On a 5+ that model suffers a Mortal Wound. This represents that model - friend, or foe - suffering the consequences of being unable to get out of the way of the Titanic model in time!

infiltrators.name: Infiltrators
infiltrators.body:
Units where every model possesses the Infiltrators keyword can be set up anywhere in No Man's Land that is at least 9" horizontally or diagonally from the edge of the enemy deployment zone that borders No Man's Land, and at least 9" horizontally and/or vertically from any enemy units already deployed using this ability.
Additionally, models with this ability ignore modifiers to their Movement characteristic when moving through Light Cover or Heavy Cover.

deep-strike.name: Deep Strike
deep-strike.body: Units where every model possesses the Deep Strike keyword can Enter the Battlefield from Strategic Reserves as detailed in the Core Activations section. However, these units can be placed anywhere on the battlefield that is at least 9" horizontally and/or vertically from any enemy units.

scout.name: Scout [X]”
scout.body: Units where every model possesses the Scouts keyword can complete a Normal Move up to [X]" before the start of the Activation Phase in Battle Round 1. If each player have units with this ability, the player with the Initiative resolves the first Scout move, and players alternate through any remaining units with Scout moves thereafter.

stealth.name: Stealth
stealth.body:
When a model with the Stealth ability is selected as the target of a Ranged attack, if the attacking model is more than 12" away, reduce the Range characteristic of those Ranged attacks by half, rounding up to the closest inch.
Further, when a unit with the Stealth ability is wholly positioned in a terrain feature with the Dense Cover keyword, that unit cannot be the target of a Ranged attack by an enemy unit that is more than 12" away. However, if the unit with the Stealth ability makes a Ranged attack from a position where they would otherwise be benefitting from this aspect of the Stealth ability, that unit loses this aspect of Stealth until the end of the Battle Round.

unyielding.name: Unyielding
unyielding.body: Models with the Unyielding keyword can use the Charge and Fight Action in an activation that began with a Fall Back.

relentless.name: Relentless
relentless.body: Models with the Relentless keyword can use the Charge and Fight Action in an activation that began with a Move action that included an advance.

fearless.name: Fearless
fearless.body: Models with the Fearless keyword never need to take a Battle Shock Test. However, these models can become Battle Shocked through rules / abilities that force a unit to become Battle Shocked.

transport.name: Transport [X]
transport.body:
Models with the Transport [X] keyword can transport a number of friendly Infantry models equal to the value of X when those models have a Toughness characteristic of 4 or less.
Each Infantry model with a Toughness characteristic of 5 count as 2 models for the purpose of this ability. Each Infantry model with a Toughness characteristic of 6 or more count as 3 models for the purpose of this ability.
Further, models with the following keywords can never embark in a model with the Transport [X] ability: Fly, Jump Pack, Hover, Mounted, Vehicle, Walker, Beast.
Models that are embarked in a Transport [X] model do not use their normal Objective Control value. Instead, each embarked model increases the Objective Control value of the Transport [X] model by 1.

firing-deck.name: Firing Deck [X]
firing-deck.body: Transport models with the Firing Deck [X] ability feature hatches, ports or open-topped designs that enable embarked models to make Ranged attacks. The [X] in Firing Deck [X] identifies how many embarked models can make Ranged attacks out of the Transport as part of their unit's activation. Units, models or wargear that identify that a model takes the place of more than 1 model for transport purposes also count as that many models for the purposes of this ability as well.

assault-egress.name: Assault Egress
assault-egress.body: Transport models with the Assault Egress ability feature assault ramps or open-topped designs that allow embarked units to quickly disembark and charge enemy units. When a unit uses the Embark or Disembark from a Transport Action to disembark from a Transport with the Assault Egress ability, that unit can then Charge and Fight.

deadly-demise.name: Deadly Demise [X]
deadly-demise.body: When a model with the Deadly Demise [X] ability is destroyed, roll a D6. On a roll of a 1 or a 6, this ability takes effect. When it does so, each unit with at least 1 model within 6" of this unit suffers [X] Mortal Wounds.

invulnerable-save.name: Invulnerable Save [X]+
invulnerable-save.body: Models with this ability possess an Invulnerable Save of [X]+, where [X] is the maximum value that their Armour Save characteristic can be reduced to. For example, a model that has a base Armour Save characteristic of 3+ is the target of an attack that has an Armour Piercing value of -3, which would reduce their Armour Save characteristic to 6+. However, the model also possesses the Invulnerable Save 4+ ability, and therefor the Armour Piercing value of the attack is superseded by this ability, allowing the model to make its Armour Save on a 4+ instead of a 6+.

feel-no-pain.name: Feel No Pain [X]+
feel-no-pain.body:
Models with this ability possess an additional saving throw made against each point of Damage inflicted on them by an enemy's attack, where the value of [X]+ determines whether that point of Damage is taken by the model with this ability.
For example, a model with a Wounds characteristic of 4 and the Feel No Pain 6+ ability is successfully wounded by an attack with a Damage characteristic of 3. The model rolls 3 dice - one for each point of Damage - and rolls a 2, 5 and 6. This means the model successfully avoided 1 of the 3 points of Damage from that attack with the roll of a 6, resulting in only 2 Damage taken and a loss of 2 of its 4 Wounds.

pistol.name: Pistol
pistol.body: Models are eligible to make a Ranged attack using a weapon with this ability even if they Advance as part of their Activation, or are in Base-to-Base Contact with enemy models.

assault.name: Assault
assault.body: Models are eligible to make a Ranged attack with this weapon even if they Advance after a Move.

heavy.name: Heavy
heavy.body:
Models making attacks with Heavy weapons do so as follows:
For Ranged attacks:
• Reduce Hit rolls by 1 and Initiative characteristic by 1 if their unit has already used the Move Action.
• Models that Move after making Ranged attacks reduce their Movement characteristic by half (rounding down), cannot use Advance Action, and reduce their Initiative characteristic by 1.
For Melee attacks:
• Reduce Hit rolls by 1 and Initiative characteristic by 1 if their unit has already used the Move Action.
These effects last until the end of the Battle Round.

rapid-fire.name: Rapid Fire [X]
rapid-fire.body: Weapons with this ability increase their Attacks characteristic by [X] when making Ranged attacks at enemy models that are half of the weapon's Range characteristic or less from the bearer.

grenade.name: Grenade
grenade.body: A maximum of 1 model in every 5 models in a unit can make a Ranged attack with a Grenade type weapon as part of a Shoot Action.

torrent.name: Torrent
torrent.body: Models making a Ranged attack using a weapon with the Torrent keyword automatically Hit their target.

one-shot.name: One Shot
one-shot.body: Weapons with this keyword can only be used once per Battle. If a model has multiples of the same One Shot weapons, only 1 of those weapons can be used per Battle Round.

precision.name: Precision
precision.body: Models making an attack using a weapon with the Precision keyword always choose a specific enemy model - including models with the Character keyword - as their target. All other criteria for a model being an eligible target (ie, line of sight) apply to this attack.

pyschic.name: Pyschic
pyschic.body: Psychic attacks are Ranged weapons available to Pysker models. A Pysker model can make 1 Ranged attack with a Pyschic weapon when it uses the Shoot Action. To do so, the model must first pass a Psychic Test (as described under the Psyker keyword). If successful, the model can proceed with the Psychic attack.

ordnance.name: Ordnance
ordnance.body:
Models are only eligible to make a Ranged attack using a weapon with the Ordnance keyword if they first Remained Stationary this Activation.
Note that Titanic models making Ranged attacks with Ordnance weapons treat that weapon as if it had the Heavy keyword instead.

indirect-fire.name: Indirect Fire
indirect-fire.body: Models can target enemy units that it cannot draw line of sight to using weapons with this keyword. When doing so, the enemy units are considered to have Light Cover. Indirect Fire attacks can never benefit from the Precision ability under any circumstances.

blast.name: Blast [X]”
blast.body:
Weapons with the Blast [X]" ability always include some amount of randomly generated attacks (in the form of D6, 2D6, D3+3, etc.) as identified in the weapon's Attacks characteristic, where [X]" determines the weapon's Blast Radius. Models making a Ranged attack using a weapon with the Blast [X]" keyword do so as follows:
• Place the Blast Marker: After selecting a weapon with the Blast [X]" keyword, place a round 25mm / ~1" marker anywhere within range and line of sight of the attacking model. The marker can be placed over enemy models, including those in base-to-base contact with friendly models.
• Determine Units Hit: Identify all units (friendly and enemy) with at least one model wholly or partially within the Blast Radius, as measured from the outer edge of the Blast Marker.
• Determine Number of Attacks: Determine the number of attacks as indicated by the weapon's profile (e.g., D6, 2D6, D3+3, etc.). For every 5 models within the Blast radius, add 1 additional attack to the total number of attacks.
• Assign Attacks to Units: Divide the total number of attacks as evenly as possible among all units within the Blast radius. Odd, additional attacks - ie, the seventh attack out of a total of 7, for example - are assigned to the unit with the most models within the Blast Radius.
• Resolve Attack Sequence for Each Unit: For each unit affected, resolve the attack sequence as normal, applying any modifiers to that specific unit from abilities affecting that unit.

beam.name: Beam [X]
beam.body:
Models making a Ranged attack using a weapon with the Beam [X] keyword do so as follows:
• Select the target unit for the attack.
• Roll to Hit.
• If the Hit is successful, use a 1" wide straight edge (ie, a tape measure, or similar) to draw a straight line between the bearer's base to any visible part of the target unit.
• Identify any units - both yours and your opponents - with at least 1 model within 1" horizontally or vertically of the straight line. Each unit that meets the above criteria suffers [X] Mortal Wounds.
• Complete the attack sequence against the target unit of the attack as normal.
Disregard step 3 if you are making an attack with a Beam [X] weapon against a unit with the Aircraft or Fly keywords.

anti-air.name: Anti-Air
anti-air.body: Models making an attack using a weapon with the Anti-Air ability increase their Ballistic Skill by 1 and count every Hit as a Critical Hit against enemy units that possess the Aircraft or Fly keywords.

sustained-hits.name: Sustained Hits [X]
sustained-hits.body: Models making an attack using a weapon with the Sustained Hits [X] ability add [X] additional Hits for each Critical Hit scored. These [X] additional Hits do not count as Critical Hits.

lethal-hits.name: Lethal Hits
lethal-hits.body: Attacks made with the Lethal Hits ability increase their Armour Penetration characteristic by 1 when that attack scores a Critical Hit.

lance.name: Lance
lance.body: Add 1 to the Wound roll each time a Melee attack is made using a weapon that has the Lance ability if the bearer attacked with this weapon as part of a Charge and Fight Action.

anti.name: Anti-[KEYWORD] [X]
anti.body: Models making an attack using a weapon with the Anti-[Keyword] [X] ability score a Critical Wound on [X]+ against enemy units that possess the corresponding [Keyword].

devastating-wounds.name: Devastating Wounds
devastating-wounds.body: Models making an attack that scores a Critical Wound using a weapon with the Devastating Wounds keyword inflict a number of Mortal Wounds equal to the Damage characteristic of the attack.

hazardous.name: Hazardous [X]
hazardous.body: Models that roll a 1 to Hit suffer [X] Mortal Wounds when making attacks using a weapon with the Hazardous ability.

poison.name: Poison [X]
poison.body: Models (excluding those with the Vehicle keyword) suffer additional Damage equal to [X] on a Critical Wound from attacks made with weapons that possess the Poison keyword.

melta.name: Melta [X]
melta.body:
A ranged attack using a weapon with the Melta [X] keyword adds [X] to that attack's Strength and Damage characteristics if the positions of the bearer and target enemy unit meet one of the following conditions:
• The bearer is within half of the weapon's Range characteristic or less from the target enemy unit, or,
• The bearer is within 9" of the target enemy unit.

harpoon.name: Harpoon
harpoon.body:
Models Hit by 1 or more Harpoon weapons reduce their Activation Points by 1 and must remain within a distance equal to the Harpoon weapon's Range from the attacking model until:
• The attacking model uses the Harpoon weapon again as part of a subsequent attack, or,
• The attacking model makes a subsequent attack of any kind.
Additionally, models Hit by 1 or more Harpoon weapons can drag attacking models, or be themselves dragged by those attacking models. This works as follows:
• If the target's Toughness is lower than the attacking weapon's Strength, the attacker can drag the target when they move, but the target must stay within the Harpoon weapon's Range.
• If the target's Toughness is equal to or higher than the attacking weapon's Strength, the target can drag the attacker when they move, but the attacker must stay within the Harpoon weapon's Range.
In instances where multiple Harpoon weapons have successfully Hit a single model, use the cumulative Strength of all attacking weapons to determine which of the above scenarios applies.
Further, Models Hit by 1 or more Harpoon weapons can complete a Charge and Fight Action against any enemy units. However, all of the above restrictions must be observed when resolving that Charge and Fight Action.

ignores-cover.name: Ignores Cover
ignores-cover.body: Enemy units that must make an Armour Save from attacks with the Ignores Cover ability never receive the benefits provided from Light Cover or Dense Cover.

ensnare.name: Ensnare
ensnare.body: Units successfully hit by a weapon with the Ensnare keyword reduce their Activation Points by 1 for the remainder of the Battle Round in addition to any other effects or damage inflicted by the weapon. These weapons have no effect on models with the Vehicle keyword.

haywire.name: Haywire
haywire.body: Vehicle models successfully hit by Haywire weapons reduce their Activation Points by 1 for the remainder of the Battle Round in addition to any other effects or damage inflicted by the weapon.

extra-attacks.name: Extra Attacks
extra-attacks.body: Models equipped with Melee weapons that have the Extra Attacks ability can make Melee attacks with any such weapons in addition to Melee attacks with a weapon that does not have this ability.

twin-linked.name: Twin-Linked
twin-linked.body:
The Twin-linked ability is never found on a weapon's profile, but instead can be added to a weapon's profile by units that offer this ability as part of their wargear options in the form of paired weapons. For example, some units may allow models to be equipped with Twin-Linked Heavy Bolters, or Twin-Linked Lightning Claws, etc. as an option among potentially others. The Twin-Linked ability makes the following modifications to a weapon's profile:
• Increase the Attacks characteristic by 1.
• Grants the Sustained Hits 1 ability, or, if the paired weapons already have the Sustained Hits [X] ability, then the value of [X] for it is increased by 1.
• If the weapon cannot have the Sustained Hits [X] ability because it is not required to make Hit rolls (ie, because it has the Torrent keyword), then the weapon's Attacks characteristic is increased by 3 instead of 1.
For example, a Twin-Linked Heavy Bolter will have 1 more attack (for a total of 4) than a single Heavy Bolter, and would have the Sustained Hits 2 ability (adding 1 to the Sustained Hits 1 ability a Heavy Bolter has as standard).
The Twin-linked ability is accessed via a Faction's Wargear Upgrades and uses a variable points cost system based on various weapon's Strength characteristic.

smoke.name: Smoke [X]”
smoke.body:
Smoke is a special form of blast attack that provides an area effect instead of damage. To complete an attack using a weapon or wargear with the smoke ability:
• Place the Smoke Marker: Place a round 25mm / ~1" marker anywhere within range and line of sight of the attacking model. The marker can be placed over enemy models, including those in base-to-base contact with friendly models.
• Leave this marker in place until the end of the Battle Round. The effect of the smoke attack lasts until the end of the Battle Round.
• Do not roll to Hit. Smoke attacks do not incur Damage of any kind, and thus no further attack sequence actions apply once the smoke marker has been placed.
For Units making Ranged Attacks near Smoke Markers: Each time a unit makes a Ranged attack that draws line of sight within [X]" of the smoke attack's marker, reduce the Ballistic Skill of that attack to 2.
For Fights:
• Each time a unit completes a Charge and Fight Action that involves moving some or all of its models within [X]" of the smoke marker, reduce the Initiative characteristic of those models by 2.
• Each time a model that is positioned within [X]" of the smoke marker is selected to Fight, reduce Hit rolls by 1.

combi-weapons.name: Combi Weapons
combi-weapons.body: Combi-weapons combine 2 or more typical weapon profiles into a single piece of wargear. When making attacks, core model type keywords of the bearer (i.e. Infantry, Monster, Vehicle, etc.) must be observed.

light-cover.name: Light Cover
light-cover.body:
• Models making Ranged attacks against units with models wholly positioned in this terrain feature reduce their Hit roll by 1. This applies when both the attacking and targeted models are wholly positioned in the same terrain feature as well.
• Reduce the Armour Piercing characteristic of Ranged attacks by 1 against models wholly positioned in Light Cover.
• Multi-model units where more than half of their models (rounding up, if needed) are not wholly positioned within a terrain feature with this keyword do not benefit from this ability.
• The benefits of Light Cover only apply to attacks that draw true line of sight to a target model (or unit) across a defined physical element of the terrain feature that has this ability. Bases or other similar flat features that mark the footprint of a terrain feature do not provide the benefits of Light Cover.
• When models making ranged attacks draw their line of sight through more than 1 terrain feature with Light Cover, the target model (or unit) instead is considered to have the benefit of Heavy Cover.

heavy-cover.name: Heavy Cover
heavy-cover.body:
• Models making Ranged attacks against units with models wholly positioned in Heavy Cover - or against models wholly positioned behind Heavy Cover - reduce their Hit roll by 1.
• Reduce the Armour Piercing characteristic of Ranged attacks by 2 against models wholly positioned in Heavy Cover.
• Multi-model units where more than half of their models (rounding up, if needed) are not wholly positioned within a terrain feature with this keyword do not benefit from this ability.
• The benefits of Heavy Cover only apply to attacks that draw true line of sight to a target model (or unit) across a defined physical element of the terrain feature that has this ability. Bases or other similar flat features that mark the footprint of a terrain feature do not provide the benefits of Heavy Cover.

vantage-points.name: Vantage Points
vantage-points.body:
• Vantage Points must be applied to any terrain feature where models can be positioned more than 5" vertically above the ground level of the battlefield.
• Infantry models making Ranged attacks from a terrain feature with Vantage Points add 1 to their Hit rolls when they are positioned more than 5" vertically above the ground level of the battlefield and are attacking a unit that is positioned at the ground level of the battlefield.

difficult-ground.name: Difficult Ground
difficult-ground.body:
• Models that move in to, out of, or through Difficult Ground reduce their Movement characteristic by 1".
• Difficult Ground has no effect for models with the Fly, Jump Pack, Hover, Phase Shift or Aircraft keywords.

impassable.name: Impassable
impassable.body:
• Impassable terrain cannot be moved over or through by any model. This does not apply to models with the Phase Shift or Aircraft keywords
• The vertical height of the terrain feature should be factored in when moving models that possess keywords that allow them to ignore certain terrain feature vertical heights (i.e., Fly, Hover).

obscuring.name: Obscuring
obscuring.body:
Any terrain feature that is at least 12" in vertical height relative to the ground level of the battlefield are considered to be Obscuring.
Models cannot be the subject of a Ranged attack if the following criteria are met:
• The target model is wholly positioned behind Obscuring terrain relative to the attacking model.
• The attacking model cannot draw true line of sight to the target model without that line of sight passing through Obscuring terrain.

exposed-position.name: Exposed Position
exposed-position.body:
• Terrain features - or parts of terrain features - that can reasonably be considered as having little or no protective features (like walls, pipes, trees, etc.), and which are at more than 5" tall relative to the ground level of the battlefield should be considered Exposed Positions.
• Models making Ranged attacks against models in Exposed Positions add 1 to their Hit rolls.

defensible-position.name: Defensible Position
defensible-position.body:
• Models positioned within a Defensible Position treat models within 2" as being in Base-to-Base contact
• Models that Charge and Fight models wholly within a terrain feature that has the Defensible Position keyword reduce their Initiative value by 1.

hill.name: Hill
hill.body:
• Hills are considered part of the battlefield's ground level. Other terrain features (such as Buildings) can be placed on Hills if the footprint of that terrain feature can be wholly within the flat surfaces of the Hill feature.
• Plain hills that are at least 5" high relative to the ground level of the battlefield, which have discernable obscuring elements (or other Terrain Features on top of the Hill, for example) should possess the Exposed Position keyword.

building.name: Building
building.body:
• Many Core Model Type keywords specify how that model can interact with Building terrain features.
• Buildings always possess the Heavy Cover keyword, and do not feature the Light Cover keyword.
• Buildings can possess the Defensible Position keyword, although it is not recommended. Players choosing to incorporate this keyword into the Building should specify areas on the Building considered to be a Defensible Position.
• Taller Buildings should have the Obscuring and Vantage Points keywords.
• Buildings with flat exposed roofs offering little or no cover (such as walls, parapets, etc.) should have the Exposed Position keyword.

ruins.name: Ruins
ruins.body:
• Buildings that have visibly suffered damage should always possess the Ruins keyword.
• Ruins always possess the Difficult Ground keyword.
• Taller Ruins should have the Obscuring and Vantage Points keywords.

forest.name: Forest
forest.body:
• Forests always possess the Light Cover keyword and can never possess the Heavy Cover keyword.
• Forests should include the Difficult Ground keyword.

craters.name: Craters
craters.body:
• Craters always include the Difficult Ground keyword.
• Craters can possess the Light Cover keyword, but can never possess the Heavy Cover keyword.

linear-low-lying-terrain-features.name: Linear, Low-lying Terrain Features
linear-low-lying-terrain-features.body:
• Smaller linear, low-lying terrain features like barricades, fortified lines, pipes, fences etc. possess the Light Cover and Defensible Position keywords.
• These terrain features should not exceed 2" in height, or 3" in width/depth. Terrain features that exceed those dimensions should be considered a different type of terrain feature.

wreckage.name: Wreckage
wreckage.body:
Wreckage is a terrain feature that is typically added to the battlefield in the place of where a Vehicle that did not suffer a Deadly Demise [X] explosion is destroyed. However, players are free to add Wreckage terrain features to their battlefield before the start of the Battle as well.
• Wreckage always possesses the Impassable keyword
• Wreckage confers the benefit of Light Cover for models wholly within 2" of the terrain feature.
